साउथ की एक्ट्रेस रेजिना कैसेंड्रा ने बॉलीवुड के बड़े बैनर पर निशाना साधा है।

एक्ट्रेस का दावा है कि Kesari 2 के प्रमोशन के दौरान धर्मा प्रोडक्शन्स ने उन्हें पूरी तरह नजरअंदाज किया।

उनका कहना है कि फिल्म के गाने में वह शुरुआत से अंत तक नजर आईं, फिर भी मेकर्स ने उन्हें टैग तक नहीं किया।

रेजिना ने जान्हवी कपूर और राधिका आप्टे की साउथ सिनेमा पर टिप्पणियों को नॉर्थ-साउथ डिवाइड बढ़ाने वाला बताया।

उनका तर्क है कि अगर किसी एक्ट्रेस को फिल्म के चित्रण से परेशानी है, तो उन्हें प्रोजेक्ट छोड़ देना चाहिए।

क्या आपको लगता है कि बड़े प्रोडक्शन हाउस वाकई साउथ के कलाकारों के साथ भेदभाव करते हैं? 🧐🔥🎬

ctx.title: Regina Cassandra questions Karan Johar for ignoring her during Kesari 2 promotions, says Janhvi Kapoor, Radhika Apte comments fuel north-south divide
ctx.summary: Regina Cassandra objected to Radhika Apte and Janhvi Kapoor's recent comments on south Indian cinema and how they create a north-south dvide.
ctx.text:
Actor Regina Cassandra has weighed in on Janhvi Kapoor's remarks about the objectification of her character in Peddi and Radhika Apte's comments about her experience working in Telugu cinema. Regina said actors who feel uncomfortable with a film's portrayal should walk away from the project if they have the choice. She also said that such conversations can create a divide between the North and South Indian film industries.
In an interview with India Today, Regina said, "I feel like at the end of the day, if they feel uncomfortable, please walk out to the film. I don’t think, we should be put in a place where we say we didn’t have a choice. This is not against a man or a woman. As a woman, it is very easy for me to take sides, I will obviously take the side of the woman, but I don’t think any of us today, especially the examples that you gave, I don’t think either of them are in a place where they can't walk out a film, especially being who they are."
Regina also spoke about her experience during the promotions of Kesari 2, in which she played the role of the film's lead Akshay Kumar's wife. She claimed that Dharma Productions did not acknowledge or tag her while promoting the film.
She said, "I really have a big issue with when a north Indian actor talks about south Indian cinema like that because you're making a north-south divide without you even realizing it and that's absolutely wrong. There are different ways of handling this. Also, Janhvi has spoken about being objectified on Karan Johar's show, the same Karan's Dharma Productions decided not to promote me in their film Kesari 2. Now, what am I supposed to call that? Objectifying what? That I'm a South-Indian? Till date I do not even know why they didn't. It is very strange. They shared that Kesari 2's song on Instagram and I am featuring in that song from start to finish, but they didn't even tag me."
Radhika Apte recently spoke about her experience working in South Indian cinema and recalled a Telugu film in which she played a woman who was married to her maternal uncle. Without naming the film, she told Zoom, "There was a Telugu film I did where I had to marry my Mama (maternal uncle) in the film. It was the most challenging film. I hated everything about it."
Janhvi starred opposite Ram Charan in Buchi Babu Sana's Peddi. Her portrayal became the subject of debate, with many criticising the camera angles and calling out makers objectification and sexualisation of her character.
She spoke about it during her apperance on Koffee With Karan. She admitted that she could have been more vigilant while filming and acknowledged that the portrayal was problematic. She called the experience "violating" and said, "I don’t like saying this because it sounds like I am shifting blame but it’s like you listen to the director and what he says. I was navigating how to make things less problematic as and when information was becoming available to me. In the south, very rarely there is a bound script. Very rarely do you see the camera angles. I should have taken advantage of my privilege. It was a violating experience in a way."
Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows.

A self-confessed cinephile who breathes Hindi cinema, Vibha can often be found sacrificing sleep after binge-watching films and web series. Though she holds a Commerce degree, she discovered her true calling in journalism after enrolling at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today.
